Project: /root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d (Node 22, built-ins only). Apply this fix list to the test files only (never edit server.mjs, package.json, public/, .team/). Spec: /root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/.team/notes/spec.md. Rules: functions under 50 lines, files under 800, no console.log, no swallowed errors, tests assert exact values. Load skill: tdd-workflow (if unavailable, ignore).

1. test/page-behaviour.test.mjs:366, :378, :387, :398 (409, fallback, no-reply, json-rejects submit tests): after the reply, assert the first log entry after the mark is ['disabled','book',false] and that it comes before the ['textContent','error',<msg>] entry, as the 201 test does around :350.
2. test/api-booking.test.mjs:48 (rule 1 content-type cases): add rejected cases (415 {error:'content type must be application/json'}) ' application/json', 'application/json ', '﻿application/json' — if Node's http client refuses a header value, send the request over a raw net socket instead (write the HTTP/1.1 request bytes yourself with Content-Length, Connection: close; header bytes for non-ASCII written as UTF-8 or latin1 — use latin1 for   (byte A0) and UTF-8 bytes EF BB BF for the BOM). Also '\vapplication/json' and '\fapplication/json' over a raw socket. Note: Node's HTTP parser may reject some of these bytes in header values with a 400 Bad Request at the parser level; if so, assert the raw reply status is not 2xx and not 415-accepting... precisely: if the parser rejects it, assert status 400 from the raw response line and note it in your report; otherwise assert 415 with the exact JSON. Put a raw-socket helper in test/helpers/server.mjs (export `rawRequest(port, bytes: Buffer) → Promise<{status:number, headers, body:string}>`) parsing status line, headers and body (Connection: close; read to end).
3. test/startup.test.mjs:130: delete `startServerOn3000`; use `startServer({ env: { PORT: value }, cwd })` from helpers (PORT: undefined removes the key; check the helper's startServer: it spreads `{PORT:'0', ...env}` so PORT: undefined overrides to undefined and buildEnv drops it — verify).
4. (Covered by 3) A failed start must reject, not resolve.
5. Move `tmp`, `FIXTURE`/`FIXTURE_BOOKING` and `listeningLine` from test/startup.test.mjs:12 and test/persistence.test.mjs:10-18/:26 into test/helpers/server.mjs as exports; remove the copies.
6. test/api-routes.test.mjs:36: reuse `assertError` from test/helpers/booking-utils.mjs instead of the local copy (adjust if signatures differ).
7. test/persistence.test.mjs:164 (sendChunked): JSON.parse inside try/catch calling reject on failure; add res.on('error', reject).
8. test/startup.test.mjs:160: make the default-DATA_FILE assertion unconditional for the temp cwd (e.g. assert.deepEqual(fs.readdirSync(dir), ['bookings.json'])); keep the repo-root check but it may stay conditional on not existing before.
9. test/startup.test.mjs:284 (no write at startup): also assert fs.statSync(file).mtimeMs and .ino unchanged.
10. test/helpers/fake-dom.mjs:140: remove unused `pending` and `nextCall`.

Then run: cd /root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d && npm test 2>&1 | tail -12 . All must pass. If any new test fails because server.mjs violates the spec, keep it strict and report expected vs actual exactly. Report changed files and the final pass/fail counts.

- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.

schema.name: Read
schema.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

content.text:
All ten fixes are in the test files only, and `npm test` passes: 282 tests, 0 failed, 0 skipped.

**Needs your attention (item 2):** Node's HTTP parser rejects a leading `\v` or `\f` in a header value with a 400 before `server.mjs` runs. Those two cases therefore assert status 400 from the raw response line, as you allowed. The NBSP cases (leading and trailing, sent as latin1 byte A0) and the leading BOM (UTF-8 bytes EF BB BF) get through the parser. They assert 415 with `{error:'content type must be application/json'}` and the JSON content type. No spec violations in `server.mjs` turned up.

Files changed, all under `/root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/test/`:
- **`helpers/server.mjs`:** now exports `rawRequest(port, bytes)`, `tmp`, `FIXTURE`, `FIXTURE_BOOKING` and `listeningLine`.
- **`helpers/fake-dom.mjs`:** removed `pending` and `nextCall`.
- **`page-behaviour.test.mjs`:** a small helper checks that the first log entry after the reply is `['disabled','book',false]` and that it precedes the `['textContent','error',msg]` entry. It is used in the 409, fallback, no-reply and json-rejects tests.
- **`api-booking.test.mjs`:** the new raw-socket cases above.
- **`startup.test.mjs`:**
  - `startServerOn3000` is gone; the test now uses `startServer({env:{PORT:value}})`. The helper's `PORT: undefined` handling works as you described.
  - The default-`DATA_FILE` check now always asserts the temp dir contains only `bookings.json`.
  - The no-write test also asserts `mtimeMs` and `ino` are unchanged.
  - The local copies of `tmp`, the fixtures and `listeningLine` were removed.
- **`persistence.test.mjs`:** `sendChunked` now wraps `JSON.parse` in try/catch that calls `reject`, and has `res.on('error', reject)`. The local copies of `tmp`, the fixtures and `listeningLine` were removed.
- **`api-routes.test.mjs`:** uses `assertError` from `helpers/booking-utils.mjs`. The shared version's `deepEqual` on the body already covers the old extra key-list check.

I also changed the "PORT means 3000" busy-port check to skip only on `EADDRINUSE` and rethrow any other error, so it no longer swallows errors. You didn't ask for that.

The `tdd-workflow` skill wasn't available, so I ignored it.
